title: Antharchy EC2 remote display: capture, streaming, and agent control
description:
## Challenge type

This initiative is an **architectural design challenge** and a **product design challenge**. It is discovery-only: no epics, stories, or tasks are attached yet.

**Updated 2026-09-03** from the storage/connectivity design conversation recorded in `chatticus-fbae4e`. Two things changed: the transport direction (worker dials out, rather than a human dialing in over SSH), and the demotion of Tailscale from an architectural component to one operator deployment option. Phase 0 validation is unaffected and stands as recorded.

## Position in the architecture

Chatticus is decomposing the original "bot" concept into three pieces:

1. **The AI agent** — conversation turns, message history, tool use
2. **The compute manifold** — routes declared work kinds to host classes (see `docs/COMPUTER_MANIFOLD.md`)
3. **Storage** — one EFS filesystem, mounted by every host class; local hosts reach it over an on-demand tunnel (see `chatticus-fbae4e`)

This initiative covers the **GUI session work kind's observe/act interface** — how agents and humans see and interact with an Antharchy desktop provisioned by the manifold. It is one work kind in the manifold, not a standalone feature.

Storage is **orthogonal** to what is displayed: the display path works the same whether `/workspace` is mounted directly (AWS host) or over the tunnel (local host). The two initiatives are not orthogonal in *transport*, however — they share one tunnel. See "Transport" below.

## Product framing

This is **not a remote desktop product.** Nobody spends hours writing code in front of this display. The primary user is the **agent**, doing the real work on the VM. Humans step in occasionally to do something manually or point something out.

The product is **agent observability plus occasional intervention:**

- Agent runs on the VM, does work (writes code, uses browser, operates apps)
- Agent or control plane can capture a screenshot at any time to show progress
- Agent can stream frames at low FPS when a human wants to watch
- Human can connect to the same session to intervene (type, click, point things out)
- Human disconnects, agent continues

A lower frame rate is acceptable. Screenshot-on-demand is the common case; a 5 FPS monitoring stream is the occasional case. No human needs 60 FPS interactive streaming.

## Problem statement

Antharchy runs headless on AWS EC2 with Hyprland (Wayland), virtual KMS, and software rendering. A live test instance (`omarchy-ec2-test`, `i-0f6c8f0c946a803e8`) proves the desktop works, but **AWS APIs alone cannot capture framebuffer pixels or inject GUI input**. EC2/SSM/CloudWatch provide lifecycle, logs, and shell at best — not a display surface.

We need agents to observe (screenshot, stream) and act (keyboard, mouse) on Antharchy desktops, with humans able to step in occasionally. WayVNC is already running on the instance and provides the complete observe/act loop today with zero new VM-side code.

Foot terminal works today. Web apps (Claude, Google Maps) fail to launch due to a separate launcher bug in Antharchy (`omarchy-launch-webapp` passes `--app=URL` to `uwsm-app`, which treats it as a filesystem path). That is a downstream dependency, not part of this initiative's design.

## Phase 0 validation (completed 2026-09-03)

All paths proven on the live `omarchy-ec2-test` instance:

| Capability | Path | Status | Evidence |
|------------|------|--------|----------|
| Screenshot | SSH + `grim` | Works | 1920x1080 PNG, verified visually — full desktop with terminals, system info, notifications |
| Screenshot | VNC framebuffer capture | Works | 1920x1080 raw pixels, 2M non-black pixels, BGRA format — real desktop content |
| Keyboard | SSH + `wtype` | Works | "hello from agent" appeared in terminal, verified via grim screenshot |
| Keyboard | VNC key events | Works | "vnc1" typed into terminal via RFB, bash tried to execute it — `command not found` |
| Mouse | SSH + `ydotool` | Works | `ydotool click 0xC0` returned exit 0 (needs input group or sudo) |
| Mouse | VNC pointer events | Sent | Click sent at 960,540 — protocol accepted |

**The entire agent observe/act loop works today via VNC, with zero new code on the VM.**

## Architecture: VNC is the v1 product

VNC is not a spike — VNC is the v1. WayVNC is already running. A programmatic VNC client (`vncdotool` in Python, or a Rust VNC library) gives an agent the complete observe/act loop in roughly 100 lines of code, with zero new VM-side infrastructure.

### Why VNC, not Sunshine or a custom API

- **Sunshine/Moonlight solves a problem this product does not have.** It exists for high-quality interactive game streaming — 60 FPS, hardware encode, low latency. The agent farm needs screenshot-on-demand and 5 FPS monitoring. Sunshine is overkill and out of scope for v1.
- **A custom WebSocket API is a v3 concern.** It is only worth building when VNC's limits are hit at scale: many agents per VM, structured events, fine-grained auth.
- **VNC gives screenshot, stream, and input in one protocol that is already running.**

### The agent display client

A thin library wrapping VNC, used by the Chatticus agent turn loop:

- `screenshot()` — single frame, on demand
- `stream(fps=5)` — low-FPS monitoring
- `type(text)`, `click(x,y)`, `key(keysym)` — input injection via VNC events

## Transport: the worker always dials out

**Changed 2026-09-03.** The previous design was `ssh -L 5900:localhost:5900 arch@<host>` — a human or the control plane dialing *into* the host. That has two problems:

1. **It cannot work for a local Antharchy VM behind a home router.** There is no inbound path, and requiring port forwarding on a home network is not acceptable.
2. **It contradicts `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**, which already commits to "the control plane never SSHs into the garage. Workers pull from SQS. Home machines need no inbound ports."

Flipping the direction unifies both host classes under one mechanism. The worker already dials out — it pulls from SQS and POSTs to the front door. Two tiers:

### Tier 1 — Observe (the common case)

Worker captures a frame (`grim` or VNC framebuffer), PUTs the PNG to S3, control plane serves the reference. This is **already how screenshots work** per `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: "Screenshots go to S3 and are referenced, not sent as bytes through the API."

Identical on EC2 and on the garage VM. Zero new transport. $0 idle.

### Tier 2 — Watch / takeover (occasional)

A "start display session" job lands in SQS. The worker opens an outbound tunnel publishing its local 5900 to an AWS-side endpoint. The control plane connects to that endpoint. VNC — framebuffer, keyboard, pointer — runs over it. Torn down when the human disconnects.

Same mechanism for EC2 and garage. No inbound ports anywhere. $0 when nobody is watching.

### Shared with the storage tunnel

Under `chatticus-fbae4e`, a local worker already brings up an on-demand WireGuard endpoint to mount EFS. **That is the same tunnel and the same endpoint.** One piece of per-org infrastructure, started when a local worker wakes, carrying both NFS and the reverse VNC channel. Building a second, display-specific transport would be waste.

For an AWS-hosted worker no tunnel is needed for storage (it is in-VPC), so Tier 2 there is a plain reverse channel to the control plane.

### Connectivity is a requirement, not a product

Per `chatticus-fbae4e` D7, the architecture states the requirement — *outbound-only, authenticated, no inbound ports on the host* — and names no vendor. Implementations are an operator deployment choice: WireGuard (default), reverse SSH (`ssh -R`, with `autossh`), SSM Session Manager port forwarding, or Tailscale/Headscale for convenience. Nothing in the Chatticus codebase imports any of them.

## Host-agnostic

| Host | Display source | Transport |
|------|----------------|-----------|
| EC2 (Antharchy) | WayVNC on localhost | Worker dials out to control plane |
| Local VM (garage Mac) | WayVNC on localhost | Worker dials out over the shared org tunnel |
| Fargate (headless) | No display | Not a GUI session work kind |

The display client is the same code in all cases; only the endpoint it is handed differs.

## Instance economics

t3.xlarge is **correct** for an agent farm, not a compromise:

- Agent farm means many VMs. t3.xlarge at ~$0.17/hr vs g4dn.xlarge at ~$0.53/hr — 3x matters at scale.
- No GPU needed: screenshot-on-demand and 5 FPS are trivially handled in software on 4 vCPU.
- GPU instance (g4dn) is a premium option for the rare case where smooth streaming matters, not the default.

This rate is also what makes the garage host worth having at all: displacing a t3.xlarge GUI session saves ~$41/month at 8 h/day, where displacing the slim Fargate computer saves ~$2.40. See the complexity budget in `chatticus-fbae4e`.

## Security model

**No VNC port is exposed on any host, to any network.** WayVNC binds localhost only. The display is the most sensitive resource on a cloud desktop and gets zero listening surface.

| Layer | Protection |
|---|---|
| Host | WayVNC on localhost; no inbound ports; no security group rule for 5900 |
| Transport | Outbound-only tunnel initiated by the worker, mutually authenticated |
| Session | Tunnel exists only while a watch session is active; torn down on disconnect |
| Authorization | v1: the SQS job authorizes the session. v3: session broker mints short-lived scoped tokens |

## Architectural design questions to refine

### Capture and transport

- VNC framebuffer capture latency on t3.xlarge — real screenshot round-trip time?
- What FPS is sustainable without starving the agent's own workload?
- Tier 2 tunnel setup latency: how long from "human clicks watch" to first frame, including endpoint start (~30 s if the WireGuard endpoint is cold — see `chatticus-fbae4e`)? Does Tier 1 cover the gap while it comes up?
- When does VNC protocol overhead matter at scale?

### Agent display client

- Python (`vncdotool`) vs Rust (custom VNC client) as the foundation?
- How does the client integrate with the agent turn loop?
- Input event mapping: VNC keysyms to Hyprland, mouse coordinates to headless output geometry.

### Security and multi-tenancy

- Session broker design: who mints tokens, how are they scoped, how do they expire?
- How do multiple agents share or isolate display sessions on one VM?
- Does the shared storage/display tunnel need per-channel authorization, or is the tunnel itself the boundary?

### Product design

- What is the user-facing promise? ("Your agents work on a real cloud desktop; you can watch and step in")
- How does a human "point things out" — shared cursor? annotations? screenshot with markup?
- What does the human dashboard look like? (grid of agent VMs with live thumbnails?)
- Pricing: per-VM, per-hour, tied to instance class?

## Explicit non-goals for v1

- **Sunshine/Moonlight** — interactive streaming, not needed for an agent farm. Separate Antharchy feature.
- **Custom WebSocket capture daemon** — premature before VNC's limits are known.
- **Frame broker for concurrent capture** — concurrent human + agent streaming is rare.
- **Clipboard sync** — not needed for agent observe/act loops.
- **Multi-seat audio** — not a concern for agent-driven VMs.
- **AWS-native display API** — does not exist.
- **A display-specific transport** — Tier 2 rides the org tunnel that storage already requires.
- **Storage** — see `chatticus-fbae4e`.

## Roadmap

### Phase 0 — Validate (completed 2026-09-03)

All paths proven on `omarchy-ec2-test`: grim screenshot, wtype keyboard, ydotool mouse, VNC framebuffer capture, VNC keyboard input.

### Phase 1 — v1 product (1-2 weeks)

- Tier 1 observe: frame to S3, served by reference. Works on both host classes immediately.
- Thin agent display-client library wrapping VNC.
- Tier 2 watch/takeover over the worker-initiated tunnel, coordinated by an SQS job.
- Fix the `omarchy-launch-webapp` bug so agents can open Claude/Maps.
- Wire the display client into the agent turn loop as a work kind in the manifold.

### Phase 2 — v2 (when v1 hits limits)

- Session broker for multi-tenant auth and short-lived tokens.
- Human dashboard: "show me what the agent sees," one-click connect.
- Operator-selectable tunnel implementations beyond the default.

### Phase 3 — v3 (scale concerns)

- Custom WebSocket API only if VNC proves insufficient at scale.
- Structured events, fine-grained auth, many agents per VM.
- GPU instance tier as a premium option.

## Success criteria

- Agent captures a screenshot on demand with <1s latency, on both host classes
- Agent streams at 5 FPS with <500ms input round-trip on t3.xlarge
- Human connects, intervenes, and disconnects cleanly
- **No inbound ports on any host, including the garage VM** — and no port forwarding required on a home router
- Many VMs runnable at t3.xlarge economics (agent farm, not streaming farm)
- Display client is host-agnostic: EC2 and local VM run the same code over the same protocol

## References

- `chatticus-fbae4e` — storage and connectivity decisions; the shared tunnel
- `docs/COMPUTER_MANIFOLD.md` — GUI session work kind
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — control plane vs worker plane, outbound-only display tunnel

comments.text: Design conversation 2026-09-03: reframed as GUI session work kind in the compute manifold. Phase 0 validation complete — VNC screenshot, keyboard, and mouse all proven on live omarchy-ec2-test instance. Storage is a separate concern (chatticus-fbae4e). Tailscale is the connectivity layer. Next step: thin agent display-client library wrapping VNC.
